newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares edge up to end at record high.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares edge up to end at record high.

text.p: Swedish shares edged up slightly on Thursday to end at a record high although prices fell back in afternoon trade.
The exchange's general index rose 0.11 percent to a record high of 2,665.98 in hefty turnover of 4.96 billion crowns.

The market was not much affected by U.S. Fed Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's warnings a day earlier and analysts said lower bond yields made investors turn to stocks. "There is so much money coming into the market," an analyst said.
"It's somewhat scary that the bourse keeps climbing despite Greenspan's comments," another analyst said.

ABB AB, the Swedish company of Swedish-Swiss engineer ABB, dropped 55 crowns to 850 after the engineer posted a group net profit for 1996 of $1.23 billion against expectations of $1.30 billion. The company also announced a 10-for-one split of ABB AB shares.
"People are disappointed by the result," said one broker. "A split usually has a positive effect but this is being overshadowed by the profit which was worse than expected."
Insurer Skandia partly rode on news about strong U.S. sales for its life insurance unit AFS and jumped 9.5 crowns to 230.5 crowns. Analysts saw overseas interest in the share.
Power company Sydkraft and defence group Celsius both released 1996 profits and both slipped. Sydkraft lost one crown to end at 144 and Celsius edged down 0.5 to 139.5.
Banking group Nordbanken recovered after falling a day earlier, up three crowns to 271.
Among sectors, the forestry group was the strongest and rose 1.55 percent.
